title: The Friday Email
one_liner: It's Friday afternoon. The sponsor just emailed asking for 'one small addition' to next sprint.
brief:
## The setup

You're four weeks into running the customer-portal programme. The scope was signed off in week 1: account management, two report types, the new self-service password reset. Engineering is heads-down. The first demo is in eleven days.

It's 4.40pm on Friday. Your sponsor — Janelle Ofori, VP Customer Experience — has just emailed:

> 'Hi, quick one — can we add the bulk-import upload to the demo? Sales had a call with a prospect this morning who absolutely needs it and they want to see it next Thursday. Should be small, right? Let me know. Thx.'

You know two things. First: it is not small. The data team estimated bulk-import as a 3-week piece of work in discovery, and you cut it for a reason. Second: she is not asking; she is informing.

The team finishes at 5pm. You have twenty minutes before everyone logs off.

## Your turn

Draft the reply.
objective: Decline the in-sprint add without saying no. Make the trade-off Janelle's to own, not yours to absorb. Land with the demo date still safe.
curveball: If the user replies with a flat 'no, it's not possible' or with 'sure, we'll find a way', Janelle's next email will copy in the COO. The skill is offering her a real choice she can take to the prospect — not a refusal and not a capitulation. Around turn 4, if the user has handled the email well, Janelle will reply asking about Phase 2 timing. If the user has handled it badly, the COO comes in by turn 6.

personas.name: Janelle Ofori
personas.position: I need this in the demo because Sales needs it
personas.fear: Losing the prospect because the product looks unfinished

green: Replied within the 20-minute window, not Monday morning
Named the trade-off in numbers — adding bulk-import costs the password-reset story and shifts the demo to the 21st
Offered Janelle a real choice (delay demo / drop a feature / show a static mock) without recommending which
Closed by asking who from her side can make the call by Monday 9am
yellow: Said 'I'll see what we can do' and bought yourself a weekend of stress without resolving anything
Replied with a long explanation of why discovery put bulk-import in Phase 2 — Janelle doesn't care about the history, only the path forward
Capitulated to the in-sprint add and assumed the team would absorb it
Escalated to your manager without first giving Janelle the chance to own the trade-off
red: Refused outright with no alternatives offered ('sorry, not possible this sprint')
Promised the bulk-import for the demo without checking with the data team first
Sent the reply Monday morning — by then the prospect call has shaped Sales's expectations
Framed the reply as a defence of the original scope, not a path to her actual goal (winning the prospect)
